content: Standard liveness/readiness split: liveness ('/health') must be trivial, no external dependency checks, no DB calls — its only job is 'is the process able to respond at all', because a failing liveness check triggers a restart, and restarting on a transient DB blip makes recovery worse. Readiness ('/health/ready') checks real dependencies (SELECT 1 with a short timeout) but must stay light — one query, short timeout (not the 1s http default when touching a DB), no checking many services serially. A failing readiness check removes the instance from traffic without restarting it. Golden rule: liveness checks the process, readiness checks whether the process can do useful work.
